name: 瀬戸内料理 雑草庵瀬戸 (Setouchi Ryori Zassouan Seto)

claims.text: Menu includes tempura (e.g., octopus tempura) and other fried items, indicating shared frying and battering with wheat flour.
Seasonal Setouchi seafood dishes are seasoned in the standard Japanese izakaya manner, relying on wheat-based soy sauce and dashi.
The kitchen is built around fish, shellfish (oysters), and meat, with fish-based dashi throughout; no separation for plant-only diets is documented.
Wheat ramen noodles are the core of nearly every dish, so a shared noodle-boiling pot and wheat-heavy kitchen make this unsuitable for strict gluten avoidance.
The broth is built on a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare that has been continuously replenished for decades; Japanese soy sauce is wheat-based.
The base broth is pork-bone (tonkotsu) and dishes include char siu pork and wontons, so animal products are integral and unavoidable.

The restaurant is fully reservation-only and course-based, and asks diners to communicate special needs (for example, smaller portions) at the time of booking, which suggests requests can be discussed in advance, though no specific allergen protocol is documented.
Emphasis on organic, natural-farming vegetables sourced from a named local farm, which may help diners discuss ingredient sourcing with the kitchen.
Fried oysters are breaded in wheat flour and deep-fried; no information indicates a separate gluten-free frying setup.
Signature anago dishes use a soy-sauce-based braising/seasoning sauce, which typically contains wheat.
Menu is built around conger eel and oysters with fish-based stocks; no vegan-safe preparation is documented.

name: 汁なし担担麺 武蔵坊 上八丁堀店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Musashibo Kamihatchobor)

claims.text: The core dish uses low-hydration wheat noodles, so wheat is central to the kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
One of the two signature styles is a soy-sauce (醤油) based tantanmen; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The dish is topped with ground pork (挽き肉) as a standard component, mixed directly into the noodles.

name: 汁なし担担麺専門 キング軒 大手町本店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Senmon Kingken Otemachi)

claims.text: Core dish uses wheat noodles plus a wheat-containing soy-sauce and sesame tare; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The shop uses a soy sauce custom-developed with a local brewing company; standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat.
The signature noodles are topped with pork mince and seasoned with a sesame/soy tare, so the dish is not plant-based.

name: 汁なし担々麺専門店 楽 小網町店 (Shirunashi Tantanmen Senmonten Raku Koamicho)

claims.text: Single-counter shop centered entirely on wheat noodles, so gluten is present throughout the cooking line; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The savory tare for brothless dandan noodles characteristically uses soy sauce, which contains wheat.
All featured dishes use chicken/pork umami and animal toppings; a shared single-counter kitchen means no separation from animal ingredients.
The menu centers on traditional Japanese seasonings including house-made soy sauce and ponzu, which are wheat-based and not gluten-free.
The kitchen is built around fish, fugu, oysters and dashi-based preparations, so cross-contact with animal products is pervasive throughout the menu.
